solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Counted on priest dressed as cardinal?

indicators.note: the priest is clothed in the cardinal's colour, so his name sits inside it

parts.note: a cardinal's robes are scarlet, so cardinal is red
Eli is the priest of Shiloh in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A priest has put on scarlet robes to pass himself off as a cardinal.
explanation.definitionFit: To have trusted or depended on something is the plain synonym here.

clue.text: End in doubt after attention was paid

indicators.note: the word End, reworked, comes after the word for attention

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

indicators.note: something in doubt is unsettled, so the letters of End are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone's attention finally drifts once the bill is settled and the result is uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was paid' must be read as one verb phrase so that it can swap with a past-tense verb meaning received in wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Money received for work is income you have earned; 'he was paid' and 'he earned' swap cleanly.

clue.text: Deals for certain work emptying tanks

indicators.note: to work something is to knead and reshape it, so the letters of certain are rearranged
emptying the word tanks takes out its middle and keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone does deals involving work that drains tanks, apparently a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' turns certain into INTERAC; 'emptying' leaves TS from tanks. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal with someone is to have dealings, engage or communicate with them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A large number hold service up for food supplier

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole construction is read from the bottom upwards
the large number holds the service within its letters

parts.note: a myriad is a vast number, literally ten thousand
the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A huge crowd keeps a church service going for someone who provides the food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' gives M-RAF-YRIAD; 'up' reads that backwards. 'service' means an armed service, not a church one.
explanation.definitionFit: A milk-producing farm supplies dairy food such as milk, butter and cheese.

clue.text: Doctrinaire Gingrich backing part of country

indicators.note: backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dogmatic US politician, Newt Gingrich, supports part of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' finds NAIREGIN; 'backing' reads it backwards. The answer is an adjective, so 'country' here means 'of the country' Nigeria.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to Nigeria, the West African state, is what this nationality adjective describes.

clue.text: Regularly inveigh against the French court's indifference

indicators.note: taking every other letter of inveigh, starting with the second

parts.note: le is the masculine form of the in French

explanation.surface: Someone routinely rails at a French court for its uncaring attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes NEG from inveigh; 'against' just sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Failure to give care or attention is the same thing as uncaring indifference.

clue.text: Heads for generous investor, vaguely expecting some presents

indicators.note: the heads of the following five words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A generous backer is hazily anticipating a few gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presents' looks like the noun gifts, but it is the verb, as in hands over.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something is to hand it over or bestow it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: God one thanks for yoghurt dish

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
I is the Roman numeral for one
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A god gives thanks for a bowl of yoghurt.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian side dish is made of yoghurt with cucumber or other vegetables.

clue.text: Son of Welsh queen that's initially nervous taking laxative

parts.note: ap means son of in Welsh names, as in ap Rhys
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual queen
i.e. stands for id est, that is

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A Welsh queen's son, a little nervous, is taking a laxative.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperient is a mild purgative medicine, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Twisting and turning script impresses Henry

indicators.note: to impress is to press into, so script has Henry pressed inside it

parts.note: handwriting or script is writing
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A twisty plot in a screenplay wins over someone called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impresses' looks like 'wins over', but it means presses H into WRITING.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to squirm and contort the body, so the participle means twisting about.

clue.text: Going round Europe, horrible daughter has face covered

indicators.note: the word for horrible goes round the letter for Europe

parts.note: vile means horrible
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A dreadful daughter touring Europe keeps her face hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: A veiled woman is one whose face is concealed by a veil.

clue.text: Very much depressed in the end, getting old

indicators.note: the end of depressed is its final letter

parts.note: early can mean ancient or old, as in early man

explanation.surface: Someone is feeling very low by the end, now that they are getting on in years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To love someone dearly is to love them greatly, an adverb of degree.

clue.text: City still very happy

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
static means still or motionless

explanation.surface: The city remains extremely cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district; its postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in ecstasy is overwhelming joy, so the adjective means overjoyed.

clue.text: Sensitive appendage regularly stroked

indicators.note: taking every other letter of stroked, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A sensitive limb is caressed at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit of the foot is an appendage, and a ticklish, sensitive one.

clue.text: Beating regularly ahead, so tries to stick around

indicators.note: the word for stick goes around the regularly picked letters

parts.note: cement is a glue, so to cement is to stick

indicators.note: taking every other letter of ahead so tries, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Someone tries to stay around despite a regular thrashing coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' runs across three words, ignoring the gaps between them; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A beating as punishment is chastisement, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Lay down tulips, frantically worried

indicators.note: frantic motion jumbles the letters of tulips

parts.note: ate, as in what's eating you, means worried

explanation.surface: A gardener plants tulips, anxious and frantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantically' makes STIPUL from tulips. 'Lay down' looks like a gardener's instruction, but it means set as a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay down a condition is to specify or demand it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: "Could" draws in the most powerful

indicators.note: the word for draws goes in the word for could

parts.note: might is the past of may, as could is of can
ties are drawn games

explanation.surface: A sentence about what the strongest could achieve, with quotation marks to mislead.
explanation.walkthrough: MIGH-TIES-T. The quotation marks make 'Could' look like a word under discussion; it is just a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Mighty means powerful, so the superlative means strongest of all.

clue.text: Ford salesman's negative reply — breathe evenly turning it all over

indicators.note: every piece put together is then read from the end back to the start

parts.note: a polite shop assistant might answer no, sir

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters of breathe, second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A car dealer refuses, taking steady breaths while mulling everything over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly' takes RAH from breathe; NO SIR + RAH is read backwards. Ford is the actor, not the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Harrison Ford is the actor famed as Han Solo and Indiana Jones.

clue.text: Hints May's ego ruined by reply!

indicators.note: ruined letters are wrecked and rebuilt into another order

explanation.surface: Clues suggest Theresa May's ego was destroyed by a retort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' shuffles all of HINTS, MAYS and EGO; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation urging someone to respond, to speak up and give an answer.

clue.text: Allowed one to enter wood

indicators.note: the letter for one goes inside the word for allowed

parts.note: OK means approved or allowed
a means one, as in a dog

explanation.surface: Someone was given permission to go into a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Oak is a hardwood timber, so it is an example of wood.

clue.text: Quite short friend

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, a tot
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A fairly small companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun: a short drink of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite in the sense of completely or entirely, as in quite right.

clue.text: Watch keeps dog safe

indicators.note: the word for watch keeps the dog within its letters

parts.note: to see is to watch
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A guard dog on watch keeps things protected.
explanation.definitionFit: Secure means free from danger, protected, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Mad drugs

definitions.meaning: an eccentric or crazy person, used as an adjective meaning daft
crack cocaine plus cannabis: two drugs side by side

explanation.definitionFit: A crazy, eccentric person is a crank; the word also splits into two drug names.

clue.text: Complaint about ring — I hate it

parts.note: c, circa, means about
O is ring-shaped
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone moans about a ring, declaring they loathe it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' looks like a grumble, but it is an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can mean a minor illness, and a chesty bark is one.

clue.text: Rubbish quiet playwright

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish dramatist

explanation.surface: A dismissal of a playwright who writes nonsense quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of contempt, much like saying nonsense when dismissing something.

clue.text: Frees cricket teams to part ways with business

indicators.note: the cricket teams separate from the business, which is taken out

parts.note: English first-class cricket is played between county sides
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A sponsoring firm releases cricket teams by ending its deal.
explanation.walkthrough: English first-class cricket is played between counties, such as Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo the knots on something is to release it, so the verb means sets loose.

clue.text: Are new chums the same?

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated a

indicators.note: making chums new reshapes their letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether new friends are the same as old ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are' looks like a verb, but it is the unit of land area.
explanation.definitionFit: Equally, in identical amount: doing as much means doing the same.

clue.text: Don't mention what could be caught on holiday

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places one piece after the other

parts.note: leave is time off work
in cricket a batter is out if caught

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about the bug you picked up while travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what could be caught' suggests an illness; it is cricket: a caught batter is out.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to not mention it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Worrying why no tea is coming

indicators.note: worrying at something tugs it about, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone frets over why no tea is arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: Something en route is approaching, so it is coming.

clue.text: Book describes the Royal Guards

indicators.note: the words describes the Royal guard the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A book describes the Royal Guards regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guards' looks like soldiers, but it is a verb: the letters span describES THE Royal.
explanation.definitionFit: This Old Testament book tells of the Jewish queen of Persia.
